english: An integer $n$ is chosen at random from $\{1,2,3,\dots,100\}$. Let $p$ be the probability that $n$ is divisible by at least one of the numbers $6$, $10$ and $15$. Then the value of $100p$ is ______.
hindi: समुच्चय $\{1,2,3,\dots,100\}$ से एक पूर्णांक $n$ यादृच्छया चुना जाता है। माना कि $p$ इसकी प्रायिकता है कि $n$ संख्याओं $6$, $10$ तथा $15$ में से कम से कम एक से विभाज्य है। तब $100p$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Every pair has lcm $30$ ($\mathrm{lcm}(6,10)=\mathrm{lcm}(10,15)=\mathrm{lcm}(6,15)=30$), and so does the triple; each intersection has $\left[\dfrac{100}{30}\right]=3$ elements
solution_full: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be the events that $n$ is divisible by $6$, $10$, $15$ respectively. All $100$ choices are equally likely, so $p=\dfrac{n(A\cup B\cup C)}{100}$.

Divisible by two of them means divisible by their lcm: $\mathrm{lcm}(6,10)=30$, $\mathrm{lcm}(10,15)=30$, $\mathrm{lcm}(6,15)=30$. Divisible by all three: $\mathrm{lcm}(6,10,15)=30$. So each pairwise intersection and the triple intersection is the set $\{30,60,90\}$ with $3$ elements.
Inclusion-exclusion (addition theorem for three events): $n(A\cup B\cup C)=16+10+6-(3+3+3)+3=26$.

Check by direct listing: the $16$ multiples of $6$, plus the multiples of $10$ not divisible by $6$ ($10,20,40,50,70,80,100$: $7$), plus the multiples of $15$ divisible by neither ($15,45,75$: $3$): $26$.
originality_note: New: three divisors chosen so that every pairwise lcm equals the triple lcm, so all four intersection terms are the same set and the inclusion-exclusion collapses to n(A)+n(B)+n(C) - 2*3 (way 4: a hidden coincidence of intersections). Closest known: 'divisible by 2, 3 or 5 from 1 to 100' and 2021-P2-Q17 (multiple of 3 or 7). Different because: the divisors are not coprime, so the student must use lcms and notice that the pair and triple intersections coincide.
blueprint_concepts: Addition theorem for two and three events
Probability using the principle of inclusion-exclusion

concept_use.Addition theorem for two and three event: P(A U B U C) is computed with the addition theorem for three events.
concept_use.Probability using the principle of inclu: The intersections are counted through lcms and combined by inclusion-exclusion; all four intersection terms equal {30, 60, 90}.
